title: Yang–Mills and the Mass Gap over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The lattice determinations of $m(0^{++})/\sig$ for $\SU(3)$: the $r_0$ route with two inputs, $3.70(6)=5.73(9)\times0.6462(30)$ and $3.63(10)=4.21(11)/1.160(6)$, and the direct continuum extrapolation $3.405(21)$ with the first scalar excitation $5.855(41)$, a spread of $9\,\%$; $T_c/\sig=0.6462(30)$ ($\SU(3)$), $0.7091(36)$ ($\SU(2)$); the $r_0$ masses of $0^{++}$, $2^{++}$, $0^{-+}$ and $0^{++*}$.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The colour factors measured at LEP: $C_A=2.89\pm0.21$ and $C_F=1.30\pm0.09$ from the four-jet angular correlations, $C_A/C_F=2.22\pm0.11$ from the jet multiplicities.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The strong coupling at two laboratory scales, $\alpha_s(M_Z)=0.1180(9)$ and $\alpha_s(m_\tau)=0.312(15)$, with the thresholds $M_Z$, $m_b$ and $m_\tau$.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The one-loop coefficient $b_0=\frac{11}{3}C_A-\frac43T_Fn_f$ and, for the confrontation of P2 only, the two-loop coefficient $b_1=102-\frac{38}{3}n_f$. The paper imports the forms; the structure of the one-loop coefficient as a sum over the field species is the import A12, and its two rationals are the frame's (C13).

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The laboratory instances: the Subjects $\p=13$, $173$, $1549$ with their Carriers $\Om=233$, $30089$, $2408561$, and the sweep over the $21$ shells $\p=4\kap+1$ below $200$. The three Carriers are $5$ modulo $12$ (B5). The unitary frame's centre has order three where $3$ divides $\p+1$, on the Subject $173$ and $12$ of the $21$ shells.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Four results of the framework: time is the drive (a theorem), mass is winding rate with masslessness as drive-invariance, confinement is the wrap of $\Om$-hard quark residues into exact hadron residues, and the gauge sector has one $\Om$-hard scale.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: Wilson's lattice gauge theory: the plaquette action on the hypercubic lattice, its strong-coupling character expansion, and the area law $W(A)=c_3^{A}$ at strong coupling, whose chart reading is the tension $a^{2}\sigma=-\ln c_3$ in lattice units, within the expansion's convergence.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: Two results of the interactions paper: the character lift (near the identity the frame's character equals the compact group's, to the stated order; the lift's parametrisation is imported as it stands and is not unitary as it stands, its repair the interactions paper's) and the order $\gcdop(3,q+1)$ of the centre of $\SU(3,\F_q)$.

rows.label: A9
rows.predicate: Steinberg's restriction theorem with the linkage principle: for the finite frame and $a+b+2\le\p$, the invariants of $\mathbf3^{\otimes a}\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}^{\otimes b}$ are the algebraic group's, hence the compact multiplicities (degrees to $8$ for $c_3$, $9$ for $c_8$; every Subject above $11$); the integer multiplicities verified on $\SU(3,\F_2)$ over $\F_4$ to degree four (C9).

rows.label: A10
rows.predicate: Casimir scaling of the string tension at intermediate distance, $\sigma_8/\sigma_3=C_A/C_F=\frac94$, the lattice's observation; a bounding value of the tension parameter of C8.

rows.label: A11
rows.predicate: The $0^{++}$ channel of the strong-coupling expansion for $\SU(3)$: $am=-4\ln u-3u+9u^{2}-\frac{27}{2}u^{3}-7u^{4}-\frac{297}{2}u^{5}+\frac{858827}{10240}u^{6}+\frac{47641149}{71680}u^{7}$ in $u=c_3$; its coefficients are rationals of the same multiplicities as $c_3$, not recomputed here.

rows.label: A12
rows.predicate: The one-loop coefficient as a sum over the field species of a paramagnetic spin term and a diamagnetic charge term, $b_0=\sum(-1)^{2s}\bigl[(2s)^{2}-\frac13\bigr]T(R)$, one complex scalar, one Weyl fermion and one real vector each counting once. The form of the sum is imported; its two rationals are computed in C13.

rows.label: A13
rows.predicate: Finite Schur--Weyl duality: over a field with more than $r$ elements the slot permutations span the commutant of $\mathrm{SL}(V)$ on $V^{\otimes r}$ (Benson--Doty, Cor.~4.4); the characteristic-free first fundamental theorem: the algebraic group's tensor invariants are spanned by the pairing-and-determinant tensors (de Concini--Procesi); the good-filtration count: tensor products of $V$, $V^{*}$ have good filtrations, their invariants the compact singlet multiplicity (Jantzen II.4.16, 4.21). For C15.

rows.label: A14
rows.predicate: Green's theorem: for a finite group and a representation over $\bar\F_q$, the sum of the images under a fixed identification $\iota$ of the eigenvalues is a virtual complex character (Green 1955); the central convolution by it, taken with the group's mean, acts on the $\chi$-block of $\C[G]$ as $a_\chi/\chi(1)$ with multiplicity $\chi(1)^2$. For C19, C20.

rows.label: A15
rows.predicate: The generic character table of $\SU(3,q)$ (Simpson and Frame 1973; CHEVIE): eight class types with centralizer orders and ten character families in the parameter $q$; verified at import by brute force at $q=2,3$ and by the orthogonality relations at nine $q$. For C19, C20, C23.

blocks.title: The finite theory and its readings

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: A registration of a state by its frame is a line of the state's space that every frame element maps to itself; the residue is the number of such lines: photon $2$ (the split torus: two invariant lines with nontrivial characters, no fixed vector), gluon $0$ (the adjoint), baryon, meson and glueball $1$ (one fixed line each). Falsifier: a registered state of residue $0$.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: [chart] The chart's scale is read on the drive: a registered scale is a nonzero element $w$ of the Subject, two scales differ by the power $n$ with $\gen^{n}=w_2/w_1$, and the chart's $\ln(\mu_2/\mu_1)$ is read as $n\ln\gen$ within one window of the drive (a wrap adds $(\p-1)\ln\gen$). The registration $\mu\mapsto w$ is the quantum paper's readout, not computed here.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The finite theory is the transfer form of lattice gauge theory along the drive: a ring of plaquettes; the tally is the frame's mean over the rungs of the amplitudes (B4), its paired weight registered once; the gap: the transfer tally's second eigenvalue over its first. [chart]: counts of frame moves above $\Om\sim10^{123}$, the hypercubic lattice (A7), the wrap operator (C8), the scale (B2).

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The spectral amplitude of a plaquette: $M=\operatorname{lcm}(q^{2}-1,q^{2}-q+1)$, a chosen identification $\iota$ of the roots of unity of order dividing $M$ in $\F_{q^{6}}$ with the powers of $\zeta_M$; for $U=U_sU_n$ by powers, $w(U)=\sum_j\iota(\lambda_j)$ over the eigenvalues of $U_s$; a configuration's amplitude $\prod_\square w(U_\square)$, a tally's paired weight $Z\bar Z$. The configurations and the registered quantity are B3's.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Colour is the Carrier's. Its triality is the Carrier's relation $\Om\equiv5\pmod{12}$, so $x^{2}+x+1$ has no root modulo $\Om$. Every Subject reads colour in its unitary frame, $\SU(3)$ over its own extension, a type that the realisation takes from the relation. Falsifier: a registered state on which the triality acts nontrivially, or colour factors off those of a unitary frame of degree three (P1).

rows.label: X5
rows.predicate: [chart] Why the finite theory needs no ultraviolet renormalisation and the continuum chart does: every tally of the finite theory is a mean over a finite frame (B3), so nothing diverges; the finite matching of the substrate's one scale to the chart's scales is $\Om$-hard (Z1), and the chart's counterterms are its account of that matching.

blocks.title: The paper's three predictions, with their falsifiers and their present confrontations

rows.label: P1
rows.predicate: The colour factors of the strong interaction are $C_A=3$, $C_F=\frac43$, $C_A/C_F=\frac94$ (C4). Falsifier: a measured $C_A/C_F$ outside $\frac94$ beyond its error. Confrontation: LEP's $2.89(21)$, $1.30(9)$, $2.22(11)$ (A2), each within one standard deviation.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:colour}; rests on A2, C4\newline \pywit{yangmills}{p46023}{P1}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p46023}{P1} \lean{FRC.YangMills.casimirs, FRC.YangMills.colour\_factors\_within}
rows.name: colour_factors_prediction

rows.label: P2
rows.predicate: [chart] Between laboratory scales $1/\alpha_s$ is linear in $\ln(\mu/\mu_0)$ with slope $b_0/2\pi$, $b_0$ the window rational (C5, A4). Falsifier: a measured $1/\alpha_s(\mu)$ off the linear law beyond the imported two-loop correction. Confrontation: one loop gives $\alpha_s(m_\tau)=0.279$ against $0.312(15)$, $2.2$ standard deviations below; with the imported $b_1$ the run gives $0.313$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:running}; rests on A3, A4, C5\newline \pywit{yangmills}{p46024}{P2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p46024}{P2}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p46024}{P2} \lean{FRC.YangMills.running\_one\_loop, FRC.YangMills.b0\_values, YangMills.two\_loop\_tau, YangMills.one\_loop\_tau}
rows.name: running_prediction

rows.label: P3
rows.predicate: [chart] The radial ratio of the operator form: $E_1/E_0\approx1.49$ for every $a$ and $\varkappa$, a property of the form of C8 and of every state the one-body wrap describes. Falsifier: such a state's first radial ratio measured off $1.49$. Confrontation: $1.54(11)$ (1999) agrees; $1.72(2)$ (2020) excludes $1.49$ by ten standard deviations under first-order error propagation at any correlation: the form fails for the glueball.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:radial}; rests on A1, C8, C12\newline \pywit{yangmills}{p46043}{P3}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p46043}{P3}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p46043}{P3} \lean{FRC.YangMills.radial\_ratio, YangMills.radial\_ratio\_confrontation}

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: The one scale of the gauge sector, $\sig$, which fixes $\LQCD$ up to a sub-horizon ratio, is $\Om$-hard: no bounded observer computes its absolute value, its ratio to the Planck energy. The paper reads its numeral from the lattice ($\sig\approx420$--$460$~MeV [import]). Every dimensionless quantity of the sector is a sub-horizon ratio.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
C1.doc: 46:C1, 46:X1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the norm-one cycle fixes no line of the shell plane, and the cycle fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the norm-one cycle, is never registered alone.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.scalar_of_im_zero
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the two scalars `±1` are the only norm-one elements with `b = 0`: `a² = 1` forces `a = ±1`.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.split_fixed_lines
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the split torus `diag(g, g⁻¹)` fixes exactly the two coordinate lines of the projective line: a point `[x : y]` is fixed iff `g x · y = x · g⁻¹ y`, i.e. `(g² − 1) x y = 0`, i.e. `x y = 0` since `g² ≠ 1` (the drive is primitive of order `p − 1 > 2`). The photon's two helicities, residue `2`.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.centre_sweep
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the arithmetic of the centre's order formula. Given that the centre of `SU(3, 𝔽_q)` is the norm-one cube roots of unity, `gcd(3, q + 1)` of them (27-fields Proposition su3, imported, not proved here), on every shell of the sweep below `200`, `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` gives `Z₃` and `q ≡ 1 (mod 12)` the trivial centre, and the residue `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` is exactly `q ≡ 1 (mod 4)` (a shell) with `q ≡ 2 (mod 3)` (the centre of order three). Kernel-decided over the range, so that no library lemma on `gcd` or `%` (which carry `propext`) enters.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.lab_centres
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the laboratory Subjects: `173 ≡ 5 (mod 12)` has the centre `Z₃`; `13` and `1549`, both `≡ 1 (mod 12)`, have the trivial centre.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.full_centre_sweep
C2.doc: 46:C2 — of the `21` shells `p = 4κ + 1` below `200`, the `12` with `p ≡ 5 (mod 12)` carry the centre `Z₃` and the other `9` do not.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.carrier_triality
C2.doc: 46:C2, 46:B5 — colour's triality is the Carrier's relation: each of the three laboratory Carriers is `5 (mod 12)`, so `3` divides `Ω + 1` and not `Ω − 1`. The cube roots of unity are the pairs `(0, 1)` and `(−1, −1)` of residues, `a + bω` with `ω² = −ω − 1` and the norm `a² − ab + b²`: both have norm `1`, `(0, 1)² = (−1, −1)` and `(0, 1)·(−1, −1) = (1, 0)`. The product of `(a, b)` and `(c, d)` is `(ac − bd, ad + bc − bd)`.

C3.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
C3.doc: 46:C3, 46:X2 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.

C4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimirs
C4.doc: 46:C4, 46:X4, 46:P1 — the Casimirs of the unitary frame with denominators cleared: `2N C_F = N² − 1` gives `6 C_F = 8` (`C_F = 4/3`), `C_A = N = 3`, `2 T_F = 1`, and `C_A / C_F = 2N² / (N² − 1)` gives `8 (C_A/C_F) = 18` (`9/4`).

C4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimir_exponents
C4.doc: 46:C4 — the Casimir rationals from the frame's torus exponents, with no lift (round 03, 9 November 2026). A torus element of the unitary frame acts on the fundamental with the eigenvalue exponents `(a, b, −a−b)` and on the adjoint with their six differences and two zeros; the second moment of the adjoint's exponents is six times the fundamental's, `2((a−b)² + (2a+b)² + (a+2b)²) = 6(a² + b² + (a+b)²)`, which is `T_A/T_F = 6` and hence `C_A/C_F = 9/4`. On the Subject `13` the split torus has the exponents `(n, 12n, −13n)` modulo `168`: `2((11n)² + (14n)² + (25n)²) = 6(n² + (12n)² + (13n)²)` for every `n < 168` (`1884 n² = 6 · 314 n²`); at `n = 1` likewise on `173` (`(1, 172, −173)`) and `1549` (`(1, 1548, −1549)`). The identity for every exponent pair is the Mathlib cell `YangMillsML.casimir_exponents_all`.

C4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimir_exponents_all
C4.doc: 46:C4 — `YangMillsML.casimir_exponents_all`: the Casimirs from the frame's torus exponents for every exponent pair, `2((a−b)² + (2a+b)² + (a+2b)²) = 6(a² + b² + (a+b)²)`, so `T_A/T_F = 6` and `C_A/C_F = 9/4` with no lift; the core decides it on the three Subjects.

C5.name: FRC.YangMills.b0_pos
C5.doc: 46:C5 — `b₀ > 0` for every `n_f ≤ 16` (the sign the chart calls asymptotic freedom, for the matter content `n_f ≤ 16`).

C5.name: FRC.YangMills.b0_neg
C5.doc: 46:C5 — `b₀ < 0` for every `n_f` from `17` to `200` (a bounded sweep, kernel-decided).

C6.name: FRC.YangMills.drive_exponent
C6.doc: 46:C6 — every winding rate `w ≠ 0` is one power of the drive: `w = gⁿ` for some `n < p − 1` (the discrete logarithm of 26-pnp, `FrameCore.eq_pow_of_ne_zero`).

C6.name: FRC.YangMills.drive_exponent_add
C6.doc: 46:C6 — the exponent of a product is the sum of the exponents, read modulo `p − 1`.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.moments
C7.doc: 46:C7 — the moment lists `(ex k)` and `(exc k)` for `k < 8`, from the Pieri multiplicities.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.c3_fractions
C7.doc: 46:C7 — the eight fractions of `c₃` modulo `β⁸`, from the multiplicities of `moments`.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.c3_readback

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.c2_lab
C7.doc: 46:C7 — `SU(2)`'s `β/4 − β³/96 + β⁵/1536` against `2T`'s `β/4 − β³/96 + β⁵/1280` on the three laboratory Subjects: the same coefficients through `β³`, the first difference at `β⁵`.

C9.name: FRC.YangMills.adjoint_two_sheets
C9.doc: 46:C9 — the two multiplicity identities of the adjoint wrap: the `β¹` coefficient of the adjoint plaquette coefficient vanishes (`E[χ²χ̄] + E[χχ̄²] − E[χ] − E[χ̄] = 0`, no singlet in `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟛` or `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟛̄`), and `4 E[(χχ̄ − 1)(Re χ)²] = 2` (`E[χ³χ̄] + 2E[χ²χ̄²] + E[χχ̄³] − E[χ²] − 2E[χχ̄] − E[χ̄²] = 2`), so `c₈ = β²/288 + …`, the square of `c₃`'s `β/18` up to the factor `9/8`: the adjoint wrap is two fundamental wraps. Stated on the sixfold multiplicities `moment6`.

C10.doc: 46:C10 — `α_s(√σ) ∈ (1.0065, 1.0075)`, `C ∈ (3.015, 3.025)`, the Herbst values `2/π ∈ (0.636, 0.637)` and `4/π ∈ (1.273, 1.274)`; `C` exceeds both, and in the form without division, `π² > 6 ln 2` on the brackets (`L² > 6 (s + t)`).

C10.name: FRC.YangMills.herbst_real
C10.doc: 46:C10 — `YangMillsML.herbst_real`: the declared coupling `2π/(9 ln 2)` in `(1.0065, 1.0075)`, `C = 3α_s` in `(3.015, 3.025)` above `4/π` above `2/π`.

C10.name: FRC.YangMills.fixed_point_couplings
C10.doc: 46:C10 — `YangMillsML.fixed_point_couplings`: the couplings `2π/(3 ln 2E)` at the chart's fixed points `E = 3.541`, `3.085`, `2.611`, all below `4/π`, the last within `0.5 %`.

C11.name: FRC.YangMills.plaquette_values
C11.doc: 46:C11 — `YangMillsML.plaquette_values`: the plaquette channel's `m/√σ` at `u = 0.06`–`0.30` with `Real.log`: `6.6`, `5.9`, `5.3`, `4.8` at order seven, and the orders' disagreement at `u = 0.30`.

C12.name: FRC.YangMills.wrap_family
C12.doc: 46:C12 — the six values read `2.232, 3.157, 3.348, 3.157, 4.464, 4.735` (each within half a unit of its decimal); none lies inside any determination's error; every member is at least `0.057` from every central value, the distance of `(a, ϰ) = (1, 9/4)` from the direct value, which it falls below by `1.7 %` (`57/3405 ∈ (0.0165, 0.0175)`).

C12.name: FRC.YangMills.wrap_family_values
C12.doc: 46:C12 — `YangMillsML.wrap_family_values`: the six family values `√(aϰ) E₀` with `Real.sqrt` from the chart's `E₀ = 2.232`, none inside a determination's error, the nearest `1.7 %` below `3.405`.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.spin_traces
C13.doc: 46:C13 — the spin term `(2s)² = −2 Tr(J₁₂²)`: `4` on the vector, `1` on the Weyl spinor (`−Tr((iσ₃)²) = 2`, the generator doubled), `0` on the scalar, with `i = 5, 80, 88` the square roots of `−1` on `13`, `173`, `1549`.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.faulhaber_third
C13.doc: 46:C13 — the Faulhaber identity `3 Σ_{k<N} (N − 2k − 1)² = N (N² − 1)` for every `N < 400` in the integers: the leading coefficient `1/3` is the chart's `∫₀¹ (1 − 2x)² dx`, the lower term `−1/(3N²)` is what the chart discards.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.faulhaber_residues
C13.doc: 46:C13 — on the shell `173` the identity holds as residues for every `N < p`, `Σ = N(N² − 1) · 3⁻¹`.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.complete_cycle_vanishes
C13.doc: 46:C13 — the complete cycle `N = p` vanishes on `13`, `173`, `1549` (the power sums over the shell vanish), while `N = 10` on `173` reads `330 = 10 · 99 / 3`: the third is never a complete residue sum, only the leading coefficient read in the window.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.hughes_nielsen_sum
C13.doc: 46:C13 — the species sum with the denominators cleared: `3 b₀ = C_A (3·(2s_V)² − 1) − n_f · 2T_F · (3·(2s_W)² − 1)` with `(2s_V)² = 4`, `(2s_W)² = 1`, `C_A = 3`, `2 T_F = 1` is `33 − 2 n_f`, the window rational `threeB0` of 46:C5, for every `n_f ≤ 200`.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.faulhaber_third_all
C13.doc: 46:C13 — `YangMillsML.faulhaber_third_all`: the Faulhaber identity `3 Σ_{k<N} (N − 2k − 1)² = N (N² − 1)` for every `N`; the core proves it for `N < 400` and as residues on the shell `173`.

C14.name: FRC.YangMills.series_window
C14.doc: 46:C14 — the series' window, the corollary of A9 (the push on T06, 9 November 2026). The `β^k` coefficient of `c₃` is built from the invariant counts of degree `≤ k + 1` (`exc k` has degree `k + 1`, `ex k` degree `k`), so on a Subject `p`, where the frame's counts equal the compact ones through degree `p − 2` (A9), the frame's series equals the compact one through `β^{p−3}`: `β^{10}` on `13`, `β^{170}` on `173`, `β^{1546}` on `1549`, all beyond the `β^7` computed. Decided on the shell `13`: raising the degree-`8` count `exc 7` by one leaves the coefficients of `β^0`…`β^6` unchanged and moves `β^7`; and the instance's departure at degree `5` (`M(4,1) = M(1,4) = 4` against `3`, so `exc 4 = 20` against `15`) puts the instance's `β^4` coefficient at `0`, where the compact one is `−5/93312` (`c3Targets`), a nonzero residue on the shell; the five decisions are the Boolean `windowCheck`.

C15.name: FRC.YangMills.frame_window
C15.doc: 46:C15 — on the shell `13`: the four rows of the binomial table are the proof's pattern; the weights `(25, 11, 11)` of `v_13`'s words are unequal, with `25 − 11 = 14 = p + 1`; the first departure lies in `[26, 49]` on `13`, `[346, 689]` on `173`, `[3098, 6193]` on `1549`; the series' window is `β^{24}, β^{23}` on `13`, beyond the `β^{7}` computed; and `4q − 3` is `5`, `9` at `q = 2, 3`.

C16.name: FRC.YangMills.spectral_amplitude
C16.doc: 46:C16 — the conductors `M = lcm(p² − 1, p² − p + 1)` on the Subjects, their gcds with the Carriers' cycles `Ω − 1`, the non-split orders `p² − p + 1` prime to the cycles (`157` against `232` on the Subject `13`), the centre of order `3` on `173` only; and in `Z[ζ₃]` the singular identity `2η + η⁻² = 3η` for `η = z, z²`, the conjugation `z ↦ z²`, `z³ = 1`, `z ≠ 1` and `1 + z + z² = 0`.

C17.name: FRC.YangMills.instance_amplitude
C17.doc: 46:C17 — the instance's distribution: the values `3, 3z, 3z²` on `64` elements each and `0` on `24` sum to zero, `64 · (3 + 3z + 3z²) = 0`; every nonzero value has norm `9`, so the moments are `192 · 9 / 216 = 8`, `192 · 27 / 216 = 24` (the cubes of `3, 3z, 3z²` are all `27`) and `192 · 81 / 216 = 72`; the invariant counts the moments are set against are `1, 1, 2`.

C18.name: FRC.YangMills.instance_transfer
C18.doc: 46:C18 — the transfer tally on the instance, the step of one plaquette with the frame's mean: the multiplicities `9, 36, 144, 27` of the eigenvalues `2/3, 1/6, 0, −1/3` sum to `216`; the eigenvalues are the integers `144, 36, 0, −72` of the matrix `216 K` over `216`; with the denominators cleared by `6` the trace is `tr K = 3`, and by `36` it is `tr K² = 8`, which is the sum `192 · 9` of the norms of the `216` amplitudes over `216`; `(3x + 1)(6x − 1)(3x − 2) = 54x³ − 27x² − 9x + 2`, so the annihilating polynomial has distinct roots; and `−1/3 < 0`.

C19.name: FRC.YangMills.subject_spectrum
C19.doc: 46:C19 — the transfer tally on the Subjects: the orders `811 273 008`, `802 332 524 681 473 968`, `33 144 476 289 365 359 469 790 000` of the frames on `13`, `173`, `1549`; the degrees `157, 2198, 2352`; `29 757, 5 177 718, 5 207 472`; `2 397 853, 3 716 672 150, 3 719 070 000`, whose inverses with the signs `+, +, −` are the eigenvalues of the step with the frame's mean; and the bookkeeping of the spectrum on each.

C19.name: FRC.YangMills.degree_identity
C19.doc: 46:C19 — the identity `Σ a χ(1) = 3 = w(1)` swept over `1 ≤ q ≤ 2000`.

C20.name: FRC.YangMills.ring_gap
C20.doc: 46:C20 — the gap of the transfer tally is `1/(q + 1)` on the seven frames of 46:C19: `1/14`, `1/174`, `1/1550` on the Subjects.

C21.name: FRC.YangMills.spectrum_in_pi
C21.doc: 46:C21 — the spectrum in `2π = p − 1` on the three Subjects, `π = 6, 86, 774`: `d₁ = 4π² + 2π + 1`, `d₂ = (2π + 2) d₁` and `d₃ = 8π(π + 1)²`, so the gap of the transfer tally is `1/(2π + 2)`; and `2π + 2` has the residue `1` on the shell.

C22.name: FRC.YangMills.product_channel_counts
C22.doc: 46:C22 — the product channels, the arithmetic of the counts. The binomial inversion of the compact counts `1, 1, 2, 6, 23` gives the fixed dimensions `0, 1, 2, 8` of `8^{⊗n}` on a Subject, and of the instance's counts `1, 1, 2, 11, 92` gives `7` and `57`. A fixed subspace of dimension `2` has `p² + 1` invariant lines, `170`, `29930`, `2399402` on the Subjects; on the instance `(4^d − 1)/3` gives `5`, `5461`, `21845` for `d = 2, 7, 8`; and the degree `8` lies in the window `2p − 1` of the Subject `13`.

C23.name: FRC.YangMills.uniform_boundary_tally
C23.doc: 46:C23 — the tally of the ring with the same boundary links at every step, of the eigenvalues `g^{±j}, 1` and `g^{±k}, 1` with `g = 2` and `(j, k) = (1, 2)`; after `n` steps the boundary classes are those of `x = 2^n` and `y = 4^n`. (1) The inverses of `2` and `4` on the three Subjects. (2) On `13` the tally at the lengths `1` to `12`. (3) On the Subjects `13`, `173`, `1549` the tally is the five powers at every regular length of the drive's cycle. (4) The other lengths: four on each Subject, the multiples of `3`, `43` and `387`. (5) At the length of the cycle the boundary links are units and the tally is `3`. Every product is reduced at once; the largest numeral formed is the degree `(p + 1)²(p − 1)`.

X1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
X1.doc: 46:C1, 46:X1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the norm-one cycle fixes no line of the shell plane, and the cycle fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the norm-one cycle, is never registered alone.

X1.name: FRC.YangMills.adjoint_no_invariant
X1.doc: 46:X1 — the adjoint has no invariant: `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` has one singlet (the trace) and the adjoint `𝟠` is its complement, `E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`; with `no_shell_eigenvalue` (the torus fixes no line) no registration singles a gluon out.

X2.name: FRC.YangMills.residue_series_pieri
X2.doc: 46:X2 — one invariant line each: baryon `E[χ³] = 1`, meson `E[χχ̄] = 1`, glueball `E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, by the Pieri multiplicities.

X2.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
X2.doc: 46:C3, 46:X2 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.

X4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimirs
X4.doc: 46:C4, 46:X4, 46:P1 — the Casimirs of the unitary frame with denominators cleared: `2N C_F = N² − 1` gives `6 C_F = 8` (`C_F = 4/3`), `C_A = N = 3`, `2 T_F = 1`, and `C_A / C_F = 2N² / (N² − 1)` gives `8 (C_A/C_F) = 18` (`9/4`).

X4.name: FRC.YangMills.colour_factors_within
